### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-app-github`, `@objectstack/connector-mcp`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via HERE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `887472c6ce223462181ccc8b9ece3c04830b5ac3` — the merge of head `a91c84adc9210ce1edd29d87b42af40c96dbef70` into base `ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 887472c6ce223462181ccc8b9ece3c04830b5ac3 && git checkout 887472c6ce223462181ccc8b9ece3c04830b5ac3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751 a91c84adc9210ce1edd29d87b42af40c96dbef70 && git checkout -B drift-repro ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751 && git merge --no-ff a91c84adc9210ce1edd29d87b42af40c96dbef70

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ea74ebf93f8b1b955b2b77327c3a34c677d4d751` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6312fe6f3108fe588197fd5256ba041077789cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts (`credentialSent`, the `include` refusal's two branches, `credentialVerified`), packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts (the TSDoc of `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` and its `status`; no type or value changes), packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-credential.object.ts (the `status` description), content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx (the `include` paragraph, the refused-credential paragraph, two failure-table rows), packages/apps/connector-github/README.md (the Credentials paragraph), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/vitest.config.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/package.json (three devDependencies) + pnpm-lock.yaml, .changeset/28311-mcp-include-scope-hidden-tools.md; read on `main` for the marker's meaning and not reviewed: packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`isConnectorCredentialRejected` at :2450, `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` at :3166 to :3250)

Inputs: card #28311 (body, the dev note 6538998021, triage 6539260047 which routes the credentialed case to the credential path, the claim), PR #28357 (body, the docs-drift comment, the seat's hand-off 6539986174 naming the question this record must answer, the file list of 10 files, the diff of 569 lines against `main` read whole, the seven commits from the merge-base), #27401 (the precedent the hand-off cites: a marker borrowed for a case whose retry and log semantics it did not describe, sent back to the maintainer), the 71 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T06:47Z: all 71 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint UI, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Test UI (all 16), Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, Validate Package Dependencies, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Auto Label, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), UI Published Artifacts), and the tree on `main` for the marker's declared contract and the materializer's handling of it. The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); `main` moved `connectors.mdx` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` since the merge-base and the merge is clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The hand-off's question: a truthful, closed widening of the marker, not the #27401 class** - yes. The marker's declared meaning on `main` is the outcome, not the status: "neither an authoring fault nor an operational one; the upstream answered, and retrying the same value cannot change its answer", with the materializer degrading, holding a stored value as `rejected` until it is set again, the declaration changes or the process restarts, and retrying an environment or vault value on the backoff. A server that was sent the credential and lists fewer tools than `include` names is exactly that outcome: the answer was given to this credential, the same value gets the same answer, and the administrator who supplies the value is the one who can change it. The materializer's handling (`holdConnectorForRejectedCredential`, read on `main`) is the behaviour the card and triage 6539260047 prescribe for this case, so the marker is not borrowed for semantics it does not carry; in #27401 the borrowed code's backoff and "upstream unavailable" log described the case falsely, which is why it went back. The TSDoc is widened in words that name the one new raiser (an MCP server that lists only the tools a credential may use), so the contract reads true after the change; no type, value or `code` moves.
- **The predicate is the one the provider already used** - right. `credentialSent` is the former `credentialVerified` expression (`http` transport and `sendsInstanceAuth(ctx.auth)`), so the credentialed branch fires only when the instance's `auth` reached the server as a header; an `api-key` as a query parameter, a `stdio` transport, no `auth`, or a credential written into `transport.headers` (part of the declaration) keep the plain fault with a byte-identical message. The five controls pin each.
- **Status 403, and the message** - right. The server answered 2xx and refused nothing in words, and 403 is what a credential short of the scopes a resource needs is answered with (RFC 6750 section 3.1, `insufficient_scope`; GitHub's own server answers an out-of-scope `tools/call` that way). The message names the missing tools, the tools listed for this credential, and both causes with their fixes; it quotes no HTTP status and no credential (`withoutCredentialThrown` scrubs the thrown value in the materializer in any case). The dev measured that GitHub's `tools/list` answer carries no field or header about hidden tools, so "both causes" is the truthful message.
- **Downstream texts follow** - right. The `sys_connector_credential.status` description names the second way a row becomes `rejected`; the connectors page's `include` paragraph, refused-credential paragraph and two failure-table rows state the split; the GitHub README no longer says an environment-variable token stops the server, and corrects itself on which of the app's own tools GitHub hides (none: `search_issues` and `issue_read` are public-read, which the dev read at `f2a07cd1`).
- **Tests and their closure** - right. The new file runs the real provider, materializer and credential store (ObjectQL over SQLite), which is why `connector-mcp` gains three workspace devDependencies and a `vitest.config.ts` that aliases them to source (`check:test-source-alias`), disarms the console intercept and quiets the registry log through `OS_REGISTRY_LOG` (both repo gates). Nine cases: the credentialed refusal, five controls, the environment path through the materializer (degraded, listed `rejected` / `env`, recovers on a reconcile), the stored path (row `rejected`, held as `credential`, a better value recovers it), and the ablation of `if (credentialSent)` reds the three credential cases alone. The lock file carries the three links only.
- **Accept-set: nothing an author writes moves** - right. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/connector-mcp` patch, `@objectstack/service-automation` patch** - accepted. A refusal reclassified on one path, a description text; no `@objectstack/spec` entry for a TSDoc-only edit, the lane's precedent (#28346).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **A credentialed instance with a real typo in `include` now marks its stored credential `rejected`** - the message names the declaration cause, and an edit of the declaration re-attempts the instance and clears the mark on a handshake that lists every entry (`markVerified`), as the body says and the hold contract on `main` describes. A false `rejected` mark on a good credential until then is the cost of a server that cannot say which cause; named, accepted.
- **The hold log line still says "refused its credential"** - `plugin.ts` is untouched; at materialization `takeDown: false` so the dematerialize line is not reached, and the held reason is the provider's own message. Reads acceptably; a later wording card if the lane wants "refused or withheld".
- **Serial overlap** - `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` with #28346 (PASS, different sections) and #28317 (dirty against `main`); `pnpm-lock.yaml` with anything that touches it. Whichever lands second merges `main`.
- **No name approval owed** - no new key, state or code.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Nothing blocking, no should-fix on the diff.** Tried: a server that lists every tool for an under-scoped token and refuses at `tools/call` (unchanged: the call-time 403 already takes the credential path through `credentialRefusals`); an `include` of zero missing tools (the branch is not reached); a server that hides tools from an api-key sent as a query parameter (not `credentialSent`, plain fault, the administrator's fix is the declaration or moving the key to a header, which the docs' split implies). One predicate reused, one existing marker with its existing handling, the plain fault kept for every case the credential did not reach: the smallest truthful shape.

**Verdict reasoning.** The marker's contract on `main` is defined by its outcome and handling, both of which this case satisfies, and the TSDoc now names the second raiser, so the widening is truthful and closed rather than a borrowed code; the split is keyed on the predicate the provider already trusted, the message carries both causes because the server cannot tell them apart, every path is pinned on the real stack with controls and an ablation, and every check is green or skipped on a head clean against `main`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-28311-mcp-scope-hidden-tools`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibw58ehQ2gRHP2h2Puz`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a91c84adc9210ce1edd29d87b42af40c96dbef70`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts (unchanged by the delta; re-read on the new head as the contract the decision is judged against), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts (the merged `credentialSent` / `credentialVerified` next to main's `ctx.credentialHandle`, `borrowingFetch`, `discoveryTransport` and `clientFor`; the new comment), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts (the new oauth2-handle case), content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx (the conflict resolution and the `static credential` wording), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/vitest.config.ts (the conflict resolution), .changeset/28311-mcp-include-scope-hidden-tools.md (the Unchanged bullet) + packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts on the new head, read and not reviewed (`credentialRefOf` :435, the connection signature :2476 to :2484, the held skip :2534, the credential and handle resolution :2592 to :2720, `isConnectorCredentialRejected` :2799, `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` :3991 to :4068, `scheduleDeclarativeRetry` :4243), packages/types/src/connector-credential-source.ts (`callWithBorrowedCredential`, the 401 refresh-once rule)

**Delta record.** The previous record on this PR (comment 6540253498, PASS on `b6312fe6`) stands for the branch's change; this record judges only what moved the head since: merge commit `4b4a4ca8` (parents `b6312fe6` and `main` at `ea74ebf9`; two textual conflicts, `connectors.mdx` and `vitest.config.ts`; `mcp-provider.ts` auto-merged against main's #28437 at `70646157`) and commit `a91c84ad` (a comment on `credentialSent`, one test, the docs and changeset naming the grant-bearing kinds among the instances that keep the plain fault). Inputs: `git diff b6312fe6 a91c84ad` for the ten files of the PR, `git diff ea74ebf9 a91c84ad` (the branch's net change on top of the `main` it merged: 10 files, 568 insertions, 51 deletions, the same file list the PR carries), the combined diff of the merge (`git show --cc 4b4a4ca8`: hunks only in the two conflict files, none in `mcp-provider.ts`), the three versions of each conflict file, the `main`-side diff `efdddc90..ea74ebf9` for `mcp-provider.ts`, the tree at `a91c84ad` for the cited code, and the 66 check-runs on this head (read 2026-11-01T03:54Z: all 66 completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Auto Label, Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint UI, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8 shards), Test UI, Test UI (all 16 shards), Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, Validate Package Dependencies, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), UI Published Artifacts). The PR reads `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`, head repo = base repo, 10 changed files, draft. No PR comment follows 6540253498.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(1) `credentialSent` next to main's credential-handle path** - holds. On the new head the materializer hands a grant-bearing instance `credentialHandle` and leaves `auth` undefined (`plugin.ts` :2700 to :2720, :2755: `auth` is set only in the final `else`), and the provider itself refuses a handle beside a static credential or a signer as a plain configuration fault. So for such an instance `sendsInstanceAuth(ctx.auth)` is false, `credentialSent` is false, the `include` miss stays the plain fault, and `credentialVerified = credentialSent` stays false, which matches the materializer's own gate on `recordCredentialProven` (`credentialHandle === undefined`). The borrowed token travels through `discoveryTransport.fetch` (`borrowingFetch`), never through `transport.headers`, so the predicate cannot be tripped by it. The new test pins exactly this: `ctx({ credentialHandle: handle })`, transport carrying a `fetch` and no `Authorization` header, the fake server answering its anonymous list, the plain message, the client closed. Order of evaluation after the merge is as the branch intended: handle checks, discovery, the catch (401 / 403 by SDK status, else upstream-unavailable), then `credentialSent`, the `include` check, `credentialVerified`, and main's `close` wrapper (borrowed clients first) is kept.
- **The comment's four factual claims, read in `plugin.ts`** - true. (a) The path a `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` takes at materialization is `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` with `ref` and `credential` resolved from `credentialRefOf(entry.auth)` (:2592 to :2612), which for `oauth2` / `app-credential` is the client or app secret (`createGrantHandle(..., credential?.value)`, `appSecret: credential?.value`). (b) A stored one is marked `rejected` (`markRejected(stored, reason)`, :4049) and the instance held. (c) A held instance is skipped while its signature is unchanged (:2534); the signature of an `mcp` instance with connections carries only the discovery organization id (`|connections:connected:discovery:${state.discovery}`, :2483), so a reconnect of the same organization, a wider token included, leaves it held: "neither marks nor re-attempts on a reconnect" is right. (d) The token the server was sent is the connection's, which the hold path never touches. Routing the handle case to the marker would therefore have produced a false `rejected` on the client secret and a hold no reconnect lifts; keeping the plain fault is the truthful choice until the materializer has a connection-keyed route.
- **(2) Consistency with the published TSDoc on the new head** - consistent by the contract's own terms. `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` defines the marker by its outcome: "the instance is well-formed and its `credentialRef` resolved", the materializer degrades, "a stored value's row is marked `rejected`", retried on the backoff only when the value is an environment or vault one. For a handle instance the `credentialRef` value is not what the listing depended on, so that outcome would be false for it; excluding it keeps every sentence of the paragraph true for every raiser that remains. `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError`'s own TSDoc ("refused the credential it sent, or accepted it and withheld what the instance declares") and the `status` doc (403 for a `2xx` that withheld) remain true of what is raised. The one unqualified clause is the paragraph's last sentence, "an MCP server that lists only the tools a credential may use, and so leaves out a tool the instance's `include` names, is answered with this marker by the `mcp` provider": read alone it covers a borrowed token too. The factory TSDoc in `mcp-provider.ts` ("when the handshake carried no instance credential ... and as `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` when it did"), the new comment, the connectors page ("sends a static `auth` credential (`bearer`, `basic`, or an `api-key` header)") and the changeset all carry the qualification; the spec sentence does not. A should-fix on wording, below, not a contract break: no type, value or `code` moved in the delta, and the marker's defined outcome is the reason for the exclusion.
- **(3) The conflict resolutions** - nothing dropped, nothing misstated. `connectors.mdx`: the net change on top of `main` (`ea74ebf9..4b4a4ca8`) is the branch's three hunks byte-for-byte (the `include` paragraph, the refused-credential paragraph, the two failure-table rows) placed among main's new rows (`vendorPublicKeyRef`, the `signed` key, the two `alipay-v3` rows, the grant-bearing row reworded by main to the `credentialHandle: true` registration, the `authorization_code` and token-endpoint rows); main's wording of every row it changed is kept, the branch's wording of the refused-credential row is kept, the merge message says exactly this. `vitest.config.ts`: the merged file keeps main's `@objectstack/types` alias (re-anchored on the same `HERE` the branch's three use; same target), the branch's `driver-sql`, `objectql` and `platform-objects` aliases, `disableConsoleIntercept: true` and `env: { OS_REGISTRY_LOG: 'warn' }`; the two header comments are folded into one that names all four entries and both reasons; main's "and nothing else" claim is rightly gone. `mcp-provider.ts`: the combined diff has no hunk, i.e. every merged hunk is one parent's; the net diff against `ea74ebf9` is the branch's change and only that (the factory TSDoc paragraph, the `credentialSent` block, the two-branch refusal, `credentialVerified = credentialSent`), on top of main's imports, `borrowingFetch`, handle checks, `discoveryTransport`, `clientFor` and `close`.
- **The delta's prose** - right. The changeset's Unchanged bullet and the connectors page's `include` paragraph now list the grant-bearing kinds among the plain-fault cases and name the static kinds that take the credential path, which is what `sendsInstanceAuth` says; the two table rows say "a static credential". "Fails the boot" for the plain fault is the fatal-mode `fail` (:2390), as before for the other plain cases; on a reload or retry it is a skipped entry or `failDegradedConnectorInstance`, as the retry row already states.
- **Accept-set, semver** - unchanged: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, two patches; the delta adds no entry and the lock file is untouched by it.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/connector-mcp` patch, `@objectstack/service-automation` patch** - accepted, as on `b6312fe6`; the delta changes a comment, a test and prose.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Pre-existing on `main` (#28437), not widened by this PR, worth a card**: a `403` the borrowed token meets at discovery (connect, handshake or `tools/list`) is a `StreamableHTTPError` 403, so `credentialRejectionStatus` raises `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` and the materializer's hold path marks the grant-bearing instance's client-secret row `rejected` and holds it against a reconnect of the same organization, the very outcome the new comment keeps the `include` miss away from (a `401` is different: `callWithBorrowedCredential` refreshes once and ends in the seam's 503, which reads upstream-unavailable). The comment's "until the materializer has a route for it" names this gap honestly; this PR narrows the new raiser away from it and leaves the old one as `main` has it. The lane should file it against the materializer (a connection-keyed hold: mark the connection "reconnect required", re-attempt on a connect), unassigned.
- **Should-fix, wording only**: the last sentence of the `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` TSDoc in `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts` would read true on its own with one qualifier, "the tools the instance's `auth` credential may use" (or "a credential the instance sent as its `auth`"), matching the factory TSDoc and the docs. Carry it on this PR or the next touch of the file; it does not block.
- **The `rejected` mark on a good static credential with a real typo in `include`** - unchanged from the previous record's flag; the delta does not touch it.
- **Serial overlap** - `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` now merged against #28346 and #28437; `pnpm-lock.yaml` with anything that touches it. The head is clean against `main` at the read.

### ④ Design judgment
